editorial:
Imagine your dad shows up on your doorstep in LA after years of not talking, claiming he just wants to be a father again. That is exactly what happens to Sid, and it sets up a story that feels very real and relatable. You will see a lot of awkward tension and some funny moments as these two try to figure out how to be in each other's lives. It is a cozy, character-driven drama that focuses on family secrets and the weird ways parents try to make up for lost time. The vibe is mostly light, but it hits some emotional notes that will make you think about your own family.

What really works here is the chemistry between the lead actors, which makes the dialogue feel natural instead of scripted. While the story moves a bit slowly in the middle, the big reveal about why the father is actually in town keeps things interesting. If you enjoy stories about healing old wounds, you should definitely give this a try.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Sid realizes his father did not come to LA just for him, but to find a woman from his past. After a lot of arguing and honest conversations, the father finally explains his regrets. The movie ends with the two men reaching a place of forgiveness. They do not fix everything instantly, but they agree to keep trying, showing that family bonds can be repaired even after a huge lie.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family dramas and stories about forgiveness.
